prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Regional Dispatch Center (Juniper) continuously intakes, triages, dispatches, and coordinates under approved protocols; jurisdictions retain resource ownership/local policy. Juniper creates incident records, preserves reports/clarifications, tracks regional coverage, and escalates gaps. Call Taker Mara (Larkspur) confirms/repeats location before medical details, distinguishes observed/reported facts, updates records before dispatch, produces Caller Location Correction Slip, and confirms incident ID and receiving facility before destination requests. Computer Aided Dispatch Console checks maps and presents incident, priority, travel, availability, constraints, staging; verify currency. Triage Supervisor (Copperfield) reviews uncertain, conflicting, deteriorating, severe, or escalation cases; assigns/document priorities by immediacy, time sensitivity, and deterioration risk; urgent threats get highest available priority and prompt dispatch. Copperfield sends Pediatric Acuity Note, advises dispatch on demand-related repositioning, and refers unusual cases to Regional Medical Director when time permits. Regional Medical Director sets policy, advises clinical resource needs, establishes elevated-demand clinical priorities, and guides specialized/protocol destination choices; no dispatch authority. Data Quality Officer (Pebble) flags defects, audits completeness/compliance/rationales, sends Duplicate Incident Audit Memo, and routes location/status corrections operationally; cannot change priority. Ambulance Coordination Platform consolidates suitable units, retains time-stamped status/movement, and presents approved destination/instructions; selection weighs priority, clinical need, travel, capability/readiness, constraints, coverage. Juniper uses swap voucher to verify current battery readiness; queue snapshot to account for northern-entry congestion. North Gate Status Board displays latest queue/access restriction; South Gate Status Board supports access routing; state uncertainty. Dispatchers compare response times with remaining coverage before moving units. Shift Commander (Sundial) approves coverage-reducing/nonstandard exceptions, reviews coverage before staging moves, and sends Mutual Aid Release Form when neighboring service released. Hospital Liaison Desk obtains facility capacity, coordinates destination consultation using condition, transport estimate, and acceptance information; contacts Emergency Department, records outcome, communicates restrictions. ED reports capacity/access/receiving changes. Juniper evaluates consultation against acuity, transport time, coverage; correction slip reconciles destination changes. Juniper records approved alternate routes and checks reasonable critical-area coverage; crews report unsuitable routes (closure, danger, delay). Radio Coordinator (Mistral) confirms talkgroup/reachability, transmits ID/location/priority/assignment/hazards, retries unacknowledged messages, alerts supervisor; network carries

New part:
S159: The Radio Coordinator relays destination instructions to the Paramedic Crew over the Regional Radio Network.
S160: The Paramedic Crew acknowledges the destination and advises dispatch if conditions require renewed consultation.
S161: The South Gate Status Board produces the South Access Lane Notice when the south approach has a material access constraint.
S162: The South Gate Status Board displays current access information for crews approaching the receiving facility through the south entrance.
S163: The Shift Commander reviews access constraints that could affect arrival timing or safe patient transfer.
S164: The Regional Radio Network supports updates between dispatch and the Paramedic Crew while the ambulance is en route.
S165: Call Taker Mara receives the Bedside Arrival Receipt to support completion of the incident record.
S166: Call Taker Mara verifies that the recorded arrival time is consistent with the dispatch timeline and crew communications.
S167: Ambulance Unit 417 reports arrival at the receiving facility and confirms when patient handover is complete.
S168: The Emergency Department and the Paramedic Crew clarify any discrepancy in patient identity or transfer documentation before the crew clears the facility.
S169: The Data Quality Officer reviews incomplete arrival or handover fields during routine record-quality checks.
S170: The Regional Dispatch Center updates the incident status after receiving confirmation that the patient has been transferred to facility care.
S171: The Hospital Liaison Desk remains available to resolve facility-level questions that arise during or immediately after handover.
S172: The Shift Commander escalates unresolved destination or access issues through established regional coordination procedures.
S173: Surge operations begin when queue age, simultaneous high-priority calls, or staffed unit availability crosses thresholds approved by regional policy.
S174: Regional Dispatch Center monitors these indicators continuously and declares the applicable surge level when a threshold is met.
S175: Computer Aided Dispatch Console displays the current surge level and the operational constraints reported by field and facility staff.
S176: Triage Supervisor validates the declaration and confirms that call prioritization remains consistent with clinical protocols.
S177: Shift Commander assigns coordination responsibilities and reviews whether normal coverage can be maintained during the surge.
S178: Regional Medical Director provides clinical direction when demand exceeds routine triage guidance or requires a regional protocol adjustment.
S179: Hospital Liaison Desk uses the Pediatric Acuity Note to convey pediatric monitoring and destination considerations to receiving staff.
S180: Pediatric calls with concerning airway, breathing, circulation, or mental status findings receive prompt clinical escalation under approved protocols.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
